I checked every proof in the file. Most are short, idiomatic one-line simp/rw proofs (Equiv.id_map, comp_map, id_traverse, traverse_eq_map_id, naturality, and the four field proofs of isLawfulTraversable') and I saw no worthwhile simplification there; merging rw chains into a single simp (e.g. in comp_traverse) would be pure golf with no gain, so I did not flag it. The one substantive finding is the detour through an equality of Functor structures in Equiv.lawfulFunctor'. Proposed proofs are sketches: I could not run Lean, so I do not claim the replacements are verified; the map_const case in particular may need an extra Function.comp_apply/Function.comp_def in the simp set or an explicit `exact h₁ a`/`exact h₀ ...` fallback. Note also that Functor.ext (Mathlib/Control/Functor.lean:47) cannot be used here, because it needs two LawfulFunctor instances for the same Functor, one of which is exactly what is being constructed. Out of rubric scope: the stale question-comment at line 117 and the old lemma name 'lawful_functor'' in the comment at line 165 are documentation issues, not proof issues.

findings.excerpt:
have : F = Equiv.functor eqv := by
    cases F
    dsimp [Equiv.functor]
    congr <;> ext <;> [rw [← h₀]; rw [← h₁]] <;> rfl
  subst this
  exact Equiv.lawfulFunctor eqv
findings.problem: The proof does not prove the functor laws at all; it builds an equality `F = Equiv.functor eqv` by destructing the `Functor t'` structure, `dsimp`-unfolding `Equiv.functor`, splitting both record fields with `congr`, and then closing the two subgoals with the goal-order-dependent bracket list `congr <;> ext <;> [rw [← h₀]; rw [← h₁]] <;> rfl`, finally `subst`-ing the equality and reusing `Equiv.lawfulFunctor`. A reader has to reconstruct which hypothesis (`h₀` or `h₁`) belongs to which field, and has to rely on the unstated fact that `congr` emits the `map` subgoal before the `mapConst` subgoal. This is exactly the kind of opaque, order-sensitive tactic chain the proofs of `Equiv.id_map`, `Equiv.comp_map`, and `Equiv.isLawfulTraversable'` (which rewrites each law with `h₂` directly) avoid.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the three `LawfulFunctor t'` fields directly from `h₀`/`h₁` and the transported laws on `t`, mirroring the field-by-field style already used in `Equiv.isLawfulTraversable'`:

```lean
    LawfulFunctor t' where
  map_const := by
    funext a
    simp only [h₁, h₀]
  id_map x := by simp only [h₀, Equiv.id_map]
  comp_map g h x := by simp only [h₀, Equiv.comp_map]
```

Here `h₀` converts the arbitrary `t'`-`map` into `Equiv.map eqv`, after which `Equiv.id_map`/`Equiv.comp_map` (this file, proved from `LawfulFunctor t`) finish the goal, and `h₁` together with `h₀` gives `map_const`. No proof of an equality of `Functor` structures, no `cases F`, no `subst`, and no bracketed `<;>` list are needed. (If `simp only` does not fire the `Equiv.map`/`Function.comp` rewrite under the `map ∘ const` binder, the fallbacks `exact h₁ a` and `exact Equiv.comp_map eqv g h x` after the corresponding `rw [h₀]` keep the same structure. I have not compiled this replacement.)
findings.benefit: Each law's proof becomes a one-line derivation naming the hypothesis and the transported law that justify it, so the reader sees the mathematical content (rewrite along the equivalence, then apply the law on `t`) instead of a record equality argument whose subgoals are determined by `congr`'s field ordering. It also no longer depends on the shape of the `Functor` structure literal, making the proof robust to changes in that structure, and it makes `lawfulFunctor'` stylistically parallel to `isLawfulTraversable'`.
